core_obligations: Quasi-separatedness (proof lines 4587-4594): by assumption X is covered by affine opens of the form X_s, and the intersection of any two of them is affine by the intersection lemma, so the standard criterion gives that X is quasi-separated.

Set up the valuative criterion (proof lines 4596-4614): let A be a valuation ring with fraction field K and let two morphisms from Spec(A) to X agree over Spec(K); since A is local each image is contained in some affine X_s and X_t, and replacing the sections by suitable powers makes s and t sections of the same invertible sheaf.

Compare the rank one modules (proof lines 4616-4634): the pullbacks of that invertible sheaf along the two morphisms are free rank one modules over A, hence submodules of their base changes to K, and the agreement over the fraction field gives an isomorphism between those base changes; the elements corresponding to the pullbacks of s and t are generators, and the isomorphism carries one to the other, so it restricts to an isomorphism of the two free modules and the generator of the second is again a generator.

Conclude (proof lines 4634-4638): hence the image of the second morphism is contained in the affine open X_s, which is separated, so the two morphisms agree, and the valuative criterion gives that X is separated.
proof_roadmap: Get quasi-separatedness from the affineness of the intersections of the given affine opens.
Apply the valuative criterion and reduce to two morphisms from the spectrum of a valuation ring agreeing over the fraction field.
Compare the free rank one pullbacks inside their base changes to the fraction field and conclude that both images lie in a common affine open.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if a scheme X with an invertible sheaf L has, for every point, a section of some power of L whose nonvanishing locus is affine and contains the point, then X is separated (statement lines 4579-4585). The proof (proof lines 4587-4640) obtains quasi-separatedness from the affineness of intersections, applies the valuative criterion, and compares the two free rank one pullbacks of the invertible sheaf inside their base changes to the fraction field to conclude that the images lie in a common affine open. H3: a valuative argument with a module-theoretic comparison, written out in full.
